subject: RHadoop vs Revolution Analytics for familiar algorithms

messages.author: 21338b463bf47f16
messages.subject: RHadoop vs Revolution Analytics for familiar algorithms
parts:
Hello - a newbie question, so apologies for its simplicity: my team has started with Hadoop adoption recently, and want to select an analytical layer on top of Hadoop. We have been regular users of R, and I am personally pushing for an org-wide adoption of R for analysis and modeling. While my team has technical skillsets for Hive, some Pig and certainly R, we do not have the skill sets (nor do we want to at this point) that sophisticated big data programmers do.

Having said that, I'm thinking about Revolution Analytics Enterprise vs. RHadoop on our Hadoop nodes. As you can imagine, there are timing, cost, corporate policy, etc. considerations, but we will deal with that. My somewhat naive question is: for the analyst who knows R, but very little Hadoop (again, relegated to Hive), will RHadoop packages be  a hard uphill climb? I.e. if we need a version of R that enables us to leverage familiar algorithms (regressions, classifications, clustering methods), my sense is that RHadoop will require a lot more sophisticated coding that using Rev Analytics Enterprise built-in packages that do the mapreduce jobs automatically. 

I welcome your thoughts and advice.

Thanks,
Armin

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: RHadoop vs Revolution Analytics for familiar algorithms
parts: None of the RHadoop packages include analytical features as Revolution R Enterprise does, so really it's not an apple to apple comparison, it's more a fish to fishing rod comparison.
